title: Extending METR Evals to Legal and Compliance Task Domains

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Legal domains have irreversible consequences, so extending evals here has a clear safety motivation. However, the causal chain depends on whether the eval findings lead to actionable deployment constraints, which is uncertain.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires legal domain expertise to design tasks and evaluate correctness. CS students without legal background would struggle to identify what constitutes genuine legal harm. Publicly available legal datasets exist but interpreting them correctly is non-trivial.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Same scope problem as gen-0962: 15 novel evaluation tasks plus automated scoring. Additionally requires legal domain validation that CS students may not be equipped to do.
